head: 913235f3

judges.name: Judge A: the sceptical power user
Judge B: the maintainer and demo-day critic
judges.angle: the maintainer and demo-day critic, adversarial, independent

supersedes: first run: Judge A alone (Judge B returned null); this rewrite carries both judges
ranking_rule: avg user_value * (avg feasibility/5) / days; ties (<0.1) broken by lifecycle then moat_fit; days = backlog estimate unless a judge verified a smaller residual at HEAD (BL-03: 3, BL-15: 4 as the exchange_financials reframe)
kill_rule: killed by both = dead; killed by one = re-read and decided with rationale (BL-02, BL-12, BL-39, BL-55 upheld)

disagreement_resolutions.BL-15: judges scored different objects (A the exchange_financials reframe, B the row as written); panel ranks the reframe at the averaged scores; not a runner-up
disagreement_resolutions.BL-42: resolved toward B: a populated shot needs the unbuilt results extractor
disagreement_resolutions.BL-49: resolved toward B: WLD-T-5 is blocked_tier4, a Tier-4 boundary; killed by both
disagreement_resolutions.BL-54: resolved toward B for the target names: scans dominate micro-cap annual reports

rows.title: Witnessed by default

judge_a.strongest_objection: Nothing to build; the zero-token witness route and the overview disclosure the row promised are already shipped by the defect lane.
judge_a.kill_reason: Already landed at HEAD: correctness_gate.apply_witnesses runs on GET /fundamentals (routers/fundamentals.py:137) and EquityOverviewPanel renders the disagreement and witness figure in the cell tooltip. Nothing left to build but tooltip-to-inline polish.

judge_b.strongest_objection: The zero-token overview witness already exists at HEAD; building this row again re-does a fixed defect and the only delta is where the second number sits.
judge_b.kill_reason: Largely shipped by R15-DATA-004 (Stage C batch 2): routers/fundamentals.py:137 runs correctness_gate.apply_witnesses on the plain GET and EquityOverviewPanel.tsx:157-168 renders a 'flagged' chip with the exchange figure in the tooltip. The residual (exchange value inline instead of tooltip) is a half-day polish ticket, not a build.

rows.reason: Killed by both. Verified at HEAD: routers/fundamentals.py:137 runs correctness_gate.apply_witnesses on GET /fundamentals and the overview cell carries the flagged chip with the exchange figure. Only tooltip-to-inline polish remains.

rows.title: A disclosure feed you can build on

judge_a.strongest_objection: Mostly landed (180-day paged window, AttachHis, per-lane AnnouncementWindow); the residual is serving the private _kind plus dual timestamps, a one-day wire change with nothing to screenshot.

judge_b.strongest_objection: The 'silent 30-day empty 200' value claim no longer holds at HEAD; what remains is two model fields, and a feed with no UI cannot be screenshotted anyway.
judge_b.kill_reason: Shipped by R15-DATA-019 (batch 3): _BSE_ANN_WINDOW_DAYS=180 paged by count, AttachLive->AttachHis fallback, and AnnouncementWindow states the covered range. Residual (submission timestamp, SUBCATNAME as a public field) is a defect ticket.

rows.reason: Killed by Judge B, upheld. Verified at HEAD: corporate_disclosures.py:120 _BSE_ANN_WINDOW_DAYS = 180 paged by count, AttachHis fallback (:114), window stated. The residual is two Announcement fields with nothing to screenshot (both judges score demo 1).

rows.title: Reasons about you: your position and your notes in every answer

judge_a.strongest_objection: read_notes already exists and the agent can call get_portfolio; the residual is a preamble position line and a brief metric, which saves one tool call rather than an hour.

judge_b.strongest_objection: read_notes and the note excerpt already ship (R15-AGENT-020); the residual is one per-symbol position line, and a preamble line is only as good as an 8b model's attention to it.

rows.reason: The position line and a renderer-side brief card from the holdings the snapshot already carries; zero tokens, keyless, closes WLD-agent-native-ux-1. Top survivor.

rows.title: The Watch: wake sweep and a 'while you were away' card that states its blind spots

judge_a.strongest_objection: A sleeping laptop sweeps only on wake, when the user is already looking; classifier rot and small-cap boilerplate make it a babysit item at twice the S budget.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Classifier tables, two exchange JSON shapes and per-launch fan-out from a laptop IP rot fastest of anything here; a quiet small-cap demo shows an empty card.

rows.reason: The Watch is the spine's hub; M at twice the S budget and a sleeping-laptop sweep only on wake.

rows.title: Number firewall with a rupee scale witness

judge_a.strongest_objection: False orphans on legitimate multi-step arithmetic teach users to ignore the strike within a week; tolerance tuning is open-ended and M-sized.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Tolerance-tuned strikes on legitimate arithmetic train users to ignore the firewall within a week; the 8-day estimate hides a unit-header parser nobody has prototyped.

rows.reason: The scale witness is right; orphan tolerance tuning is open-ended, M.

rows.title: Page receipts

judge_a.strongest_objection: Scanned small-cap filings have no text layer, so the receipt reads 'scanned, from the aggregator' on exactly the names this product targets; S-M, not S.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Scanned BSE PDFs have no text layer, so the receipt most small-cap users see reads 'scanned: no page'; the chip is invisible until a keyed research run.

rows.reason: Page receipts read 'scanned' on the micro-caps this product targets; S-M.

rows.title: Coverage honesty: say what the app could not see

judge_a.strongest_objection: It changes no number; a user who sees 'Statements: unavailable' every day on SME names learns to ignore the strip. StatusChrome already reads provider-health, so only the brief block and strip are new.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Two surfaces for one idea: the strip is more chrome on a busy header, and a coverage block that prints every run becomes boilerplate nobody reads. Honest S only if the strip is dropped.

rows.reason: Zero-token 'what I could not see' block; Judge B: honest S only if the header strip is dropped.

rows.title: Start recording: point-in-time EOD and fundamentals observations

judge_a.strongest_objection: Nothing visible for months; a laptop closed for a week walks the archive on wake from the user's IP, and one bhavcopy format change writes silent gaps unless the marker is perfect.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Nothing to screenshot; 40 MB a year of rows no surface reads for months, and a bhavcopy format change writes gap markers no user ever sees.

rows.reason: Recorder shows nothing for months and walks the archive from the user's IP on wake.

rows.title: Tripwires: kill criteria compiled once, watched for free

judge_a.strongest_objection: No sweep exists (BL-04 unbuilt), so armed rules are checked only when the app opens, which is when the user would look anyway; the field vocabulary becomes a contract to maintain.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Depends on a Watch that does not exist; llama3.1:8b compiling prose to rules will mis-parameterise, and an 'armed' rule the user cannot inspect is false comfort.

rows.reason: Compiled kill criteria are the moat, but without BL-04's sweep they are checked only on open.

rows.title: Red Pen: paste anyone's numbers, get a marked-up verdict

judge_a.strongest_objection: Most tips are narrative, not numbers; the checker says CANNOT CHECK on the tips that matter, and the BL-05 grammar it needs does not exist (company_narrative._NUMBER_RE reads $ and K/M/B/T only).

judge_b.strongest_objection: Binding pasted claims to {symbol, metric, period} with the keyless 8b model mis-binds basis and period; a CONTRADICTED on a basis mismatch is worse than no verdict.

rows.reason: Needs BL-05's grammar; most tips are narrative and read CANNOT CHECK.

rows.title: Proof Open: the first minute is a demonstration

judge_a.strongest_objection: Marketing shaped as onboarding: the same disagreement already rides the overview tooltip, so the serious investor gains nothing after minute one; an all-agree large cap makes it look empty.

judge_b.strongest_objection: The demo decays the day an exchange lane breaks, and every keyless first run now waits ~8 s on NSE's cookie dance before the user has typed anything.

rows.reason: Two days on the witnessed GET that now exists; the best single screenshot in the set, but the serious investor gains little after minute one and it decays with an exchange lane. Runner-up 2.

rows.title: Turn receipt

judge_a.strongest_objection: The two things it claimed to expose are already exposed; what remains duplicates the transcript's tool calls and the brief's sources tray.
judge_a.kill_reason: Core already at HEAD: the composer ContextMeter and the per-message tokens/$ footer (R15-AGENT-040, ChatSidebar.tsx:1402/1543, chat-history.ts usage/spendUsd) expose cost and forgetting; the residual tools/sources/checks line is line creep.

judge_b.strongest_objection: ContextMeter, per-message usage and spend already ship (R15-AGENT-040/012); what remains is a tools/sources line that reads as a debug footer.

rows.reason: Killed by Judge A, upheld. Verified at HEAD: ContextMeter (ChatSidebar.tsx:1402/1545) and per-message spendUsd (streaming.ts:96) expose cost and forgetting; the residual tools/sources line is the line creep the row itself warns against.

rows.title: Cap-table X-ray: names, beneficial owners, encumbrance, holder counts, pledge trend

judge_a.strongest_objection: PAN is not disclosed so 'same name string' is all it can say; the BSE-only XBRL lane leaves NSE-only SME names, the target, with today's summary. M, not S.

judge_b.strongest_objection: SEBI SHP taxonomy revisions silently break the parser (it happened once already); same-name matching without PAN yields confident false identity. Pledge is already modelled (R15-DATA-023).

rows.reason: Highest value per the forensic seat, but BSE-only XBRL leaves NSE-only SME names on today's summary; M.

rows.title: Corporate-action chain

judge_a.strongest_objection: The parser it promised already landed (CorporateAction kind/ratio/ex_date across NSE+BSE, R15-DATA-025); what remains is chart markers, factor receipts and a toggle, and a wrongly applied factor rewrites price history.

judge_b.strongest_objection: R15-DATA-025 already parses bonus/split/rights with ratios from both exchanges; the residual adjusted-series toggle needs a recorder that does not exist plus canvas work.

rows.reason: Parser landed (R15-DATA-025); chart markers and a factor toggle remain, with price-history rewrite risk.

rows.title: Results-day first take (deterministic results-grid extraction)

judge_a.strongest_objection: As written (PDF grid, archetype dictionary, page receipts) it is M with four unmet deps; only the reframe onto exchange_financials (filed revenue/PAT/EPS with XBRL URL and filing date already at HEAD) is S, and it loses per-cell page receipts.

judge_b.strongest_objection: One fixture per grid layout per filer archetype is a permanent curation job; a row-matcher miss on a lender produces a confident wrong variance table.

rows.reason: Only as the exchange_financials reframe (filed QoQ/YoY with the XBRL/BSE receipt): scored as written by Judge B (feasibility 2, lifecycle 1), as the reframe by Judge A; see section 3.

rows.title: Guidance ledger: what management said against what printed

judge_a.strongest_objection: Most target small caps hold no calls; where they do, hedged language makes HIT/MISS a judgement the verbatim gate cannot make, and every transcript costs BYOK tokens. M-L.

judge_b.strongest_objection: M-L on three unbuilt substrates; transcript coverage is thin exactly on small caps, and the verbatim gate needs page receipts that do not exist.

rows.reason: Guidance ledger needs transcripts most small caps do not hold and BYOK tokens per transcript.

rows.title: Tip Ledger

judge_a.strongest_objection: The serious investor this product targets does not trade Telegram tips; a wrong resolve on a renamed SME ticker yields a confident, libel-shaped scorecard. M, writes the book.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A wrong resolve on a renamed SME ticker yields a confident wrong scorecard about a source the user trusts; corporate-action correctness becomes a forever tax.

rows.reason: Tip Ledger is for a user this product does not target; libel-shaped on a wrong resolve.

rows.title: Brief diff: ask again, see what changed

judge_a.strongest_objection: Price-derived metrics change daily so the strip is never empty; re-research is rare enough that the prior is weeks stale and 'everything changed'. Lead with filing facts or it is the wall it replaces.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Price-derived metrics change daily so the strip always says something changed; the diff is only as stable as the brief's structured keys, which vary by model.

rows.reason: Pure frontend diff strip between two briefs of the same symbol; lead with filing facts, collapse market-moved values. Runner-up 1.

rows.title: Undo and ghost edits

judge_a.strongest_objection: Undo-from-review with a pre-image already exists (proposed-changes.ts undo, status 'undone') and AUTO no longer touches data-writes; Cmd-Z and ghost rows are polish any app has.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Session undo already ships in ProposedChangesReview (R15-AGENT-041); Cmd-Z and ghost rows are polish, and ghost renderers are a per-panel tax forever.

rows.reason: Undo-from-review already exists; ghost rows are polish.

rows.title: Trust bench and 'Audit me'

judge_a.strongest_objection: Truth packs rot within a quarter and the page hands rivals copy; the user gains nothing beyond the witness flags the overview already shows. An agent-day per release of upkeep.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Truth packs rot with every rename and delisting; a committed TRUST.md whose failures never shrink is a stunt that hands rivals copy.

rows.reason: Truth packs rot quarterly and hand rivals copy.

rows.title: The Figure and the Why key

judge_a.strongest_objection: A lineage card is a tooltip with more rows; the witness verdicts it would render already ride the cell tooltip, and every metric must declare lineage forever.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Every metric must declare lineage or the card says 'not recorded', which on day one is most cards; a new primitive needs an R9 conformance review.

rows.reason: A lineage card is a tooltip with more rows; every metric must declare lineage forever.

rows.title: Evidence locker

judge_a.strongest_objection: Storing pypdf's extraction of a scanned PDF preserves garbage faithfully; 'changed under you' fires on pypdf drift unless bytes are hashed. Depends on unbuilt BL-06.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Disk growth and LRU policy for a feature most users never notice; a 'document changed' diff on scanned PDFs is unreadable.

rows.reason: Locker preserves pypdf garbage faithfully; needs BL-06 and byte hashing.

rows.title: Gatekeeper exits

judge_a.strongest_objection: The notify half needs the unbuilt Watch; only an on-open timeline card with the 180-day cluster rule over the now-paged feed stands alone, and SUBCATNAME drift needs a visible unclassified bucket.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Depends on the unbuilt Watch for the notify path; as a read handler over the 180-day feed it would be dependency-free and S, but the row as written is not.

rows.reason: Standalone on-open timeline card over the paged 180-day feed is S and dependency-free; the notify half waits for BL-04.

rows.title: Exit Door: can I actually get out

judge_a.strongest_objection: BhavRow has no delivery column; a total-volume version overstates exit capacity 2-3x on operator names, reassuring exactly when it should not. The honest version needs the recorder and the delivery fallback.

judge_b.strongest_objection: BhavRow has no delivery field and the recorder does not exist; from one cached session the glyph is a guess that reads as a sell signal.

rows.reason: Exit capacity needs delivery volume the bhavcopy row lacks; a total-volume version overstates and must wait for the recorder.

rows.title: Filing clock

judge_a.strongest_objection: FiledPeriod.filed and quarter end already give the days-to-results series, but five periods is not a trend; 'results 44 days after quarter end' is noise the user cannot act on for quarters.

judge_b.strongest_objection: The 180-day window yields two data points per name; the 3-quarter drift rule cannot fire for a year, and submission timestamps are not on the Announcement model.

rows.reason: Days-to-results series from FiledPeriod.filed; honest but slow to become actionable.

rows.title: Living model

judge_a.strongest_objection: A worse Excel: the user who keeps a model already has Excel; actuals auto-fill only for names with parseable filings and the xlsx writer is a new sidecar dependency.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A worse Excel; the xlsx writer is a new sidecar dependency against the footprint target, and it stands on an unbuilt results extractor.

rows.reason: A worse Excel with a new xlsx sidecar dependency.

rows.title: Rulebook: it holds you to your own words

judge_a.strongest_objection: It annotates, never blocks, for the disciplined minority who already keep their rules; a mis-compiled rule nags on every add. Depends on unbuilt BL-24.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Nagging by design; an 8b model mis-compiles prose rules, and the disciplined minority who write rules are the users who least need the nag.

rows.reason: Annotates, never blocks; depends on unbuilt BL-24.

rows.title: Red-flag rule packs

judge_a.strongest_objection: 'Steps matched' sequences also describe honest turnarounds; the operator reviewing every rule of every pack is babysitting by design. Three unbuilt dependencies.

judge_b.strongest_objection: The corpus is a liability: a rule firing on a real listed company reads as an accusation whatever the copy says, and the operator reviews every rule forever.

rows.reason: Rule packs need three unbuilt deps and operator review of every rule.

rows.title: Track record: the app keeps score on itself and its providers

judge_a.strongest_objection: Value accrues only from repeated briefs on the same symbol; most users never re-brief a name enough to grade anything, and no claims ledger or migration story exists in the sidecar today.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Value accrues over months and needs a results extractor to grade against; a ledger that grows forever in a repo with no migration story.

rows.reason: Value only from repeated briefs on the same name; no claims ledger exists.

rows.title: The number changed: drift ledger

judge_a.strongest_objection: Nothing to say for weeks (no recorder exists), then false alarms on TTM rolls get it muted the week it starts talking.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Needs weeks of recorder observations before it can say anything; the per-field tolerance bands tuned in month one are exactly what rots.

rows.reason: Nothing to say for weeks, then TTM-roll false alarms.

rows.title: Seven Pages: annual-report reader

judge_a.strongest_objection: Micro-cap annual reports are often scans; it reads '3 of your 7 pages' on the names it exists for, each run costs real BYOK tokens, and the AR locator endpoint is unverified.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A 250-page AR read is token-heavy and beyond llama3.1:8b; the section locator is unverified and scanned ARs dominate the target names.

rows.reason: Seven Pages costs BYOK tokens per run and reads scans poorly.

rows.title: Alerts with a track record

judge_a.strongest_objection: Alerts are what every dashboard has; the dry-run over a 180-day tape is shallow enough to be false comfort, and the tripwire engine it rides does not exist.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Generic alerts on a tripwire engine that does not exist; a shallow dry-run history is the false comfort it claims to remove.

rows.reason: Alerts with a dry-run over a 180-day tape; rides the unbuilt tripwire engine.

rows.title: Operator radar

judge_a.strongest_objection: Hand-tuned thresholds with no recorded history false-positive on every genuine re-rating; a nervous user sells winners. ASM/GSM and BSE delivery lanes are unconfirmed.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A false alarm on a genuine re-rating costs the user money; it needs the recorder, delivery data and thresholds that are all unbuilt or tuned.

rows.reason: Hand-tuned thresholds with no recorded history false-positive on re-ratings.

rows.title: Honesty card and trial ledger for backtests

judge_a.strongest_objection: Backtesting is peripheral to the witnessed-research user and it sits on an admitted critical metrics defect (COD-backtest-1); honest deflation of a number the target user never computes.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Backtesting is peripheral to witnessed research for this user; a trial ledger that punishes exploration gets switched off.

rows.reason: Backtesting is peripheral to the witnessed-research user; sits on an open critical metrics defect.

rows.title: Priced in: what the market cap already assumes

judge_a.strongest_objection: Its history column reads the vendor statements that serve another company on SME ticker collisions (DAT-P3-1 family still open, the -SM.NS gate in flight); a sensitivity grid on witnessed TTM alone is the only honest v1.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A reverse DCF is a calculator any spreadsheet has; the history column is thin for SME names via yfinance, and a sensitivity grid looks like regulated research.

rows.reason: Only a sensitivity grid on witnessed TTM is honest while the collision lane is open; Judge B calls the reverse DCF a spreadsheet calculator.

rows.title: Forkable research (.vybrief) and the receipt bundle

judge_a.strongest_objection: A file format is a forever promise for a feature retail users do not use; as a diagnostics bundle it is a zip nobody has asked for yet. Depends on unbuilt BL-05 and BL-22.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A file format is a forever promise; few individual investors share research bundles, and replay breaks the day a provider dies.

rows.reason: A file format is a forever promise for a feature retail users do not use.

rows.title: Calm protocol

judge_a.strongest_objection: Fires only while the app is open during market hours, when the sleeping-laptop user is not there; 'looks like the market' minutes before a filing lands is exactly wrong.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Only fires while the app is open in market hours on a laptop that sleeps; composes three unbuilt items.

rows.reason: Fires only while the app is open in market hours; wrong minutes before a filing.

rows.title: Instant cockpit

judge_a.strongest_objection: Speed cannot be screenshotted and the two-writer mirror is a new drift surface for a first impression that the defect lane already improved.
judge_a.kill_reason: A boot-speed cache any desktop app has; the win sits in the defect fixes (the port wait now runs on thread::spawn in lib.rs), and a mirror risks a cached price reading as live during market hours. Not demoable in a screenshot.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Fixing the boot freeze captures most of the win; the mirror adds a two-writer drift problem for a first impression the user sees once a day.
judge_b.kill_reason: Depends on COD-rust-core-1 (R15-LIFECYCLE-001), still needs_gui, not fixed: the main thread blocks ~35 s on the MCP port-wait at every cold boot, so nothing can paint early whatever is mirrored to disk.

rows.reason: Killed by both. Boot speed is not demoable in a populated screenshot or a transcript; the two-writer price mirror is a live-vs-cached drift surface; the port wait already moved off the main thread (lib.rs:316 thread::spawn).

rows.title: Earned autonomy

judge_a.strongest_objection: The product offering to stop asking is the product asking to be trusted more; polish on a fixed defect.
judge_a.kill_reason: The whitelist that carried the value already landed (AUTO_APPLIED_KINDS = panel/chart/watchlist; data-writes never auto-apply). The residual tally nudges the user toward less oversight, which the row itself names as its risk.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A 23-of-23 tally cannot be populated for a screenshot; it reads as the product nudging toward less oversight for a whitelist (autoApplies) that already exists.

rows.reason: Killed by Judge A, upheld. AUTO_APPLIED_KINDS already excludes data-writes at HEAD (src/store/agent-autonomy.ts); a 23-of-23 tally cannot be populated for a screenshot and reads as the product asking for less oversight, the row's own named risk.

rows.title: GO bar and learned routines

judge_a.strongest_objection: Bloomberg mnemonics in a product whose spine is the composer; the palette already fuzzy-matches a symbol and 'shareholding' in two keystrokes, and the routine-learning half nags.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Bloomberg mnemonics for a terminal-native minority; routine learning is nag risk and mnemonic collisions with real NSE symbols are certain.

rows.reason: Palette already fuzzy-matches; the mnemonic bar is habit for a different product.

rows.title: Page One

judge_a.strongest_objection: Three boxes of items that do not exist yet (BL-18, BL-35, BL-15); the filler scorer punishes the qualitative context small-cap research lives on.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A composition of three unbuilt items; the filler score costs an extra LLM call and punishes useful qualitative context.

rows.reason: Three boxes of items that do not exist yet.

rows.title: Pre-print card and your forecast record

judge_a.strongest_objection: Asking the user for three numbers the evening before is homework most will skip, and n<4 quarters shows nothing for a year; three unbuilt dependencies.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Everything it shows comes from two unbuilt substrates; on scanned results the print column reads 'unparsed'.

rows.reason: Homework the evening before results; n<4 quarters shows nothing for a year.

rows.title: One number, one truth

judge_a.strongest_objection: Covers only what <Fig> has adopted, which is nothing today; timing skew between panels fires more often than a real disagreement.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Only covers what <Fig> has adopted, which today is nothing; timing-skew false positives between panels.

rows.reason: Covers only what <Fig> has adopted, which is nothing today.

rows.title: Surprise without analysts (SUE)

judge_a.strongest_objection: A seasonal random walk on eight lumpy small-cap quarters gives a sigma with n=4 effective; surprise against an expectation nobody held. The vendor second source is the collision lane.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A statistic on an unbuilt extractor; a mis-extracted PAT gives a confident wrong sigma, and the vendor second source is thin on SME names.

rows.reason: Seasonal random walk on eight lumpy quarters gives sigma at n=4.

rows.title: Proceeds ledger

judge_a.strongest_objection: Issues below the monitoring-agency threshold, most micro-caps, have no MAR to parse; PDF table parsing is never four days once scans and merged cells appear.

judge_b.strongest_objection: PDF table parsing of Monitoring Agency Reports is not 'the cheapest parser'; sub-threshold small caps have no report at all.

rows.reason: Proceeds ledger needs MAR PDFs most micro-caps do not file.

rows.title: Cheap-paper calendar

judge_a.strongest_objection: LLM extraction of per-tranche lock-ins from a scanned allotment letter degrades to 'enter manually', after which the calendar holds what the user typed. Two unbuilt dependencies.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Narrow forensic audience; an LLM extraction of multi-tranche lock-in dates the user must accept once per issue, on an unbuilt Watch.

rows.reason: Lock-in extraction from scanned allotment letters degrades to manual entry.

rows.title: Peer set and read-across

judge_a.strongest_objection: A comps table is on every site; the read-across half needs typed edges the user curates by hand and reviews yearly, which is babysitting.

judge_b.strongest_objection: A comps table is any screener; edges go stale and the read-across half is pro-seat only.

rows.reason: Comps table is everywhere; read-across edges are hand-curated babysitting.

rows.title: Dodge ledger and who's in the room

judge_a.strongest_objection: Small-cap transcript coverage is thin; a deterministic DEFLECTED label on a legitimate no-guidance answer is an accusation with a rule attached.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Transcript coverage is thin on small caps; labelling a legitimate no-guidance answer as a dodge is a reputational error.

rows.reason: Deterministic DEFLECTED on a legitimate no-guidance answer is an accusation.

rows.title: User-addable MCP servers

judge_a.strongest_objection: No legitimate server to plug in and a new injection path into the main loop; extensibility DNA is not a reason to ship an empty socket.
judge_a.kill_reason: Its surviving motivating examples are screener.in scrapers the ledger says not to add; it opens a prompt-injection path (WLD-harness-context-4 still open) for a feature with no honest data source behind it.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Opens a fresh injection path for a gap the refute downgraded to medium; the app cannot audit a remote server's read-only claim.
judge_b.kill_reason: Depends on WLD-T-5 (R15-AGENT-064), status blocked_tier4: a user-controlled subprocess/tool layer is a core-architecture decision the operator has not made. Surviving motivating examples are ToS-grey screener scrapers.

rows.reason: Killed by both. Boundary: WLD-T-5 is blocked_tier4 (a user-controlled tool/subprocess layer is a core-architecture decision the operator has not made); its surviving examples are scrapers of a source the ledger says not to add; opens an injection path while WLD-harness-context-4 is open.

rows.title: Factor X-ray

judge_a.strongest_objection: A percentile over wrong fundamentals is a confident wrong percentile.
judge_a.kill_reason: Factor-exposure strips are standard portfolio-tool fare; its ranks launder the still-open statement-lane collisions (DAT-P3-1 family) into confident percentiles, and the momentum/volatility legs need months of recorded EOD that do not exist.

judge_b.strongest_objection: Nothing agent-first or witnessed about a percentile; thin BSE-only coverage renders 'unranked' for the very names this user holds.
judge_b.kill_reason: A factor-exposure strip is a feature every portfolio-analytics dashboard ships; percentile ranks over vendor fundamentals launder errors into confident numbers and the momentum/volatility legs need months of recorded EOD that does not exist.

rows.reason: Killed by both. A factor strip every portfolio dashboard ships; percentiles over the still-open statement-lane collisions are confident wrong percentiles; momentum/volatility legs need recorded months that do not exist.

rows.title: Incubator: frozen rules with an out-of-sample record
